question.text: Per NISM Ch 2.6 (Antecedents and Growth), what was the historical milestone in the 1950s-1960s that revolutionised institutional acceptance of alternative investments?

answer.text: The advancement of Modern Portfolio Theory, which established the mechanics and advantages of diversification — showing that risk from alternative investments can be diversified at the portfolio level
The launch of the Bombay Stock Exchange derivatives segment
The passing of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code in India

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 2.6, beginning with the 1950s and 1960s, modern portfolio theory made considerable advances which established the mechanics and advantages of diversification, advocating the principle that risk from alternative investments can be diversified. This Markowitz-era development allowed institutions to evaluate risky individual assets on a portfolio-contribution basis rather than standalone. The Trap: Option B — BSE derivatives came in the 2000s. Option C — IBC was 2016, relevant to special-situation funds per Ch 2.3.6. Option D — SEBI is 1992, too late for the 1950s-60s window. Note: The keyed milestone is the advancement of Modern Portfolio Theory, which provided the analytical foundation for evaluating alternative investments at the portfolio level.
